// Batch_75_1002 Books Misclassification · Outputs 1 to 4

Why Batch 75 Books came back. Where we followed the SOP, where we did not, and where Walmart's feedback disagrees with it.

// How to read this page
SOP
Walmart's rules for Books product types (PT_Classification_Definitions_Books_final.docx). Every verdict on this page is judged against it.
Step A, Step B, HLQA, RCA
The four steps every item goes through. Step A labels the item. Step B reviews the Step A label. HLQA is our last check, and its label is what we deliver. RCA is Walmart's check of a sample after delivery.
RCA feedback
What the RCA step says about each sampled item. The items it marks wrong set our score.
Our mistake
The SOP gives a clear answer and our label does not match it.
We followed the SOP
The RCA feedback marked it wrong, but our label is what the SOP says.
SOP doesn't say
The SOP does not cover the case, or the listing has too little detail to judge.

// Question 1 in detail: do our labels follow the SOP?

83% of our labels match the SOP. The mistakes come from a handful of rules.

How often each product type was labelled correctly

Each row is a product type: the type the SOP says the item should be. The blue bar is the share we delivered with that correct label. The white line is the share Step A got right, before Step B and HLQA. When the white line sits past the end of the bar, Step B and HLQA made things worse for that type. Hover a row for the counts.

Which SOP rules we miss most

Each bar counts the items that go against one rule. Dark blue: the RCA feedback caught them and marked them wrong. Light blue: the RCA feedback let them through, so they did not lower our score, but they still go against the SOP.

At which step did the wrong labels happen?

We followed each wrong label back through the three steps before delivery (Step A, Step B and HLQA) to see where it went wrong.

Outputs 2 and 3 scored lowest. Part of that is not our mistake.

This section looks only at the 455 items the RCA feedback marked wrong, and sorts each one: was it our mistake, or was our label actually what the SOP says?

Error rate per output

The share of each output's sample that the RCA feedback marked wrong; lower is better. The score on the right is 100% minus that. For Output 4, the dashed outline adds the 32 items from Walmart's second review. Hover a bar for the counts.

Who was right on the items marked wrong

Each bar is one output's errors, split three ways: our mistakes, cases where we followed the SOP and the RCA feedback did not, and cases the SOP doesn't cover. Output 4 includes the 32 from Walmart's second review.

// How we did this

What was marked wrong: the RCA feedback files for Outputs 1 to 4 (items marked Error, minus the rebuttals Walmart accepted), plus the 32 extra corrections from Walmart's second review of Output 4 on 20 Nov. The scores are Walmart's own figures.

How each item was judged: by reading the product listing (title, description, images) against the SOP, PT_Classification_Definitions_Books_final.docx. Our mistake means the SOP gives a clear answer and our label does not match it. We followed the SOP means the RCA feedback marked it wrong but our label is what the SOP says. SOP doesn't say means the SOP does not cover the case or the listing is too thin to judge. This is our reading of the SOP; Walmart has not confirmed it.

The full check for Question 1: all 6,705 sampled items, including the 6,250 the RCA feedback passed, were screened by product type (named-product guides, printed music, pages to color, fill-in products, non-book products, periodicals), and every flagged candidate was read before it was counted. Video game guides, sticker books, kits sold with a book, flash-card books and fitness trackers are left out of the percentages because the SOP does not settle them.

Step A, Step B and HLQA: from Cosmo, through Superset (gold.wrt_item_label_trajectory, batches 75-1 and 75-2), matched to 6,700 of the 6,705 sampled items. The delivered label is the one HLQA set after Step B. Step A annotators are named from their Cosmo accounts.

Product details: titles, descriptions and images come from the listing data Walmart sent with each output. Descriptions are trimmed of catalog boilerplate such as condition and binding lines.
